title: The SUM function: adding numbers
summary: SUM adds up the numbers in one or more ranges, and ignores text and empty cells inside a range.
intro: `SUM` is the most used Excel function: it adds up the numbers in one or more ranges. Instead of typing `=C2+C3+C4+C5+C6` you type `=SUM(C2:C6)`, and the result stays right if any value changes.
args: The first number, reference or range to add.
More numbers or ranges, up to 255 arguments.
examples: Adds up the sales of every product.
A range and a separate cell in one formula.
errors: You typed text directly as an argument, such as `=SUM("abc")`. Text inside a range is ignored.

faq.q: Does SUM add cells that hold text?
faq.a: No, it ignores text and empty cells inside the range and adds only the numbers.

faq.q: Can I add columns that are not next to each other?
faq.a: Yes, separate the ranges with a comma, such as `=SUM(B2:B6,D2:D6)`.
